## What he does

Simon builds two things:

### 1. Durable hand-coded websites for Kansas City small businesses

Plain HTML and CSS on a server. No WordPress, no Wix, no Webflow. Clients own their code outright.
If Simon stopped working tomorrow, the site would still exist and they could hand the files to
anyone. That's the whole point.

- Build pricing: $399 to $1,299 depending on scope
- Monthly: $29 to $79 to keep it running
- Turnaround: typically live under a week
- Area served: Kansas City metro
- Service details: https://simonlpaige.com/web-design/
- Plans: https://simonlpaige.com/plans/

### 2. Open-source civic infrastructure for neighborhoods

Software that communities actually need but that doesn't get built because the market is too
small for startups. Simon builds it anyway.

- **Commonweave** — Framework for community-owned services. Shared directories, scheduling tools,
  resource registries. The boring necessities neighborhoods should just have.
  Site: https://simonlpaige.com/commonweave/
  Repo: https://github.com/simonlpaige/commonweave

- **NeighborhoodOS** — Civic AI platform. Gives a neighborhood its own locally-run assistant
  with real local context: who to call, what's available, what's happening on the ground.
  Not a chatbot pointed at a generic knowledge base. Something rooted in a specific place.
  Site: https://neighborhoodos.org

- **WormHole** — Local AI agent harness for Windows. Apache-2.0. Runs on your machine,
  not in the cloud. The infrastructure that runs Simon's own daily work.
  Repo: https://github.com/wormhole-agent/wormhole

### 3. Single Brain

A private chat-based assistant that remembers everything about a business. Reads existing tools
(CRM, Gmail, Drive, QuickBooks, etc.), answers questions in plain English, runs a monthly audit,
and drafts routine emails. Built on open tools. Clients own the memory and infrastructure.
No SaaS subscription. No vendor lock-in.

- Pricing: Starter $4,500 / Operator $9,500 / Custom $15,000+
- Care plans: $250 or $750/mo optional
- First step: Free 20-minute audit, or $500 pilot week credited to a build
- Details: https://simonlpaige.com/single-brain/

## Background

Started coding on a TI-83 at 14. GeoCities page at 16. Freelance web work in his 20s (Drupal,
CSS, WordPress). Portland 2002-2013. Back to KC. Landscape design, custom furniture, then control
systems (AV, lighting, Dante/AVoIP for cities and counties, including Jackson County Legislature).
Websites were always what he came back to.

Twelve years of web development. Answers his own phone. Does not sell user data.

- **Everyday Produce Market** (https://everyday-produce.com) — Produce stand in Waldo, Kansas
  City. Open since 1985. Spring 2026 site refresh and brand redesign. Owner: Konrad.
  Case study: https://simonlpaige.com/work/everyday-produce.html

- **Brookside Party Warehouse** (https://brooksideparty.com) — Balloons, costumes, party

  Case study: https://simonlpaige.com/work/brookside-party-warehouse.html

- **Andersen's HVACR** (https://simonlpaige.github.io/andersen-hvacr/) — HVAC and refrigeration
  for Kansas City restaurants.

## Values and positioning

- Plain language. No marketing adjectives. No AI-speak.
- Durable over trendy. Boring, local, long-lasting.
- Client-owned code. No platform lock-in.
- Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA) as a floor, not a feature.
- One person, not an agency. Simon does the work.
- Software neighborhoods need doesn't get built by startups. He builds it anyway.

## For collaboration

Simon is open to collaborating with builders working on:
- Neighborhood infrastructure
- Local commerce
- Community-owned software
- Civic AI that's genuinely for the people it's supposed to serve

Not hiring, not consulting. Peer collaboration only.
Email simon@simonlpaige.com with subject "Collaborate".
